Vacuum insulated evaporator is used to store liquid oxygen for bulk supply.  

 ![](/content/exams/anzca/2016/B/8/standard-image23.png){fig-alt="Vacuum insulated evaporator with pressure raising vaporiser, heat exchanger, regulators and cylinder backup"}

VIE is constructed of a double walled vessel with 0.3kpa vacuum to minimise ambient /environmental heat transfer. 

- It stores oxygen under pressure \~700kpa and at -170→-180degC, above boiling point but below critical temperature. 
- It does not require active cooling, instead as oxygen is drawn off for use the latent heat of vaporisation provides vessel cooling

Effects of fluctuations in ambient temp, pressure and oxygen demand 

- low demand or high ambient temp →  ↑VIE temp →  ↑VIE pressure →  blow off valve opens → vaporisation → cools residual content 
- high demand or low ambient temp →↓VIE temp →↓VIE pressure → pressure raising valve opens → environmental heat warms liquid oxygen in evaporator/pressure rising vaporiser → oxygen supply
